pass_a_gloss: If anyone seems to be wise among you in this age, let him become a fool (cf. 1 Cor 3:18). He who cried out before says: Be foolish and senseless, that you may become wise (perhaps better Rabanus: Attend, that not only did he not cry out: Be foolish and senseless, but that you may become wise). Instead: He who cried out before have manuscripts: Solely because he did not. If therefore there is a blameworthy wisdom, according to which 'the sons of this age are wiser than the sons of light in this generation' (cf. Luke 16:8), good is God, who are wiser than the sons of light in this generation' (cf. Luke 16:8), good is God, who overturns diverse things by contraries, that he may fulfill what is said: 'His end will be foolish.' When will his end be foolish? It is necessary that Christ reign until he puts all his enemies under his feet, but when he has subjected all things to himself, 'the last enemy, death, will be destroyed' (cf. 1 Cor 15:25-26); when death has been destroyed, then the utmost parts of the partridge will be, and his end will become foolish. This is about the partridge. 4. The principle indeed of the beginning of the second chapter this reading is: 'Throne of glory exalted from the beginning place, our sanctification, our sustentation, sustentation of Israel. Lord, all who have forsaken you, let them be confounded departing, let them be written upon the earth, because they have forsaken the fountain of life, the Lord.' Isaiah the blessed prophet said (+ as manuscripts) seeing the Lord and his kingdom: 'I saw the Lord of Hosts sitting upon a throne exalted and lifted up' (Isa 6:1). He saw and Jeremiah how God reigns, therefore glorifying him he says: 'Throne of glory exalted from the beginning place, our sanctification. If you wish to understand these things concerning Christ, you will not sin, if concerning the Father, you will not think impiously: for it is indeed the throne of glory exalted and from the beginning Savior (or + is).'Throne of glory' (or + is), therefore his exalted kingdom; (or + and) 'our sanctification' the Christ is· 'For when [the] one who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are from one all. 'Patience Israel.' As self-righteousness is the savior, self-truth, self-sanctification, so self-patience. And it is not just to be without Christ nor holy without him nor to endure without having Christ. For patience of Israel himself is. And even if you refer to God, thus you do not act impiously. 'Lord, all who have left you, let them be ashamed, having departed.' Each of us when he sins, through which he sins, leaves Christ, and having left Christ leaves God. For doing injustice leaves righteousness and becoming profane leaves sanctification mine and waging war leaves peace and being under the enemy becomes leaves the redemption and being outside the wisdom of God being leaves wisdom. Therefore all who leave God the prophet curses, teaching us what will happen to them, saying 'All who leave you, let them be ashamed.' As far as they have withdrawn, let them be ashamed so much. 'Let them be written upon the earth.' All men are written: the holy in heaven, but the 'rejoice because the names are said to the disciples under the,' but the sinners upon the earth. Your names are written in the heavens. Therefore it is necessary to rejoice, if such a one becomes, that his name may be written in the heavens. As the name of the saints is written in the heavens, so of those who live earthly, those who do not traverse the earth Edom but those who have the fields of Edom and the vineyards, the names are written as those leaving God upon the earth. 'Let them be ashamed' for he says 'having departed, upon the earth let them be written.' For 'with what measure you measure, it will be measured to you.' Each is the cause to himself of being written. Then if you seek upon the earth, you do not seek the heavenly things. If your soul has inclined toward these things, you yourself become the cause, of Jesus saying 'Do not store up for yourselves treasures upon the earth upon the earth, where moth and consumption destroy, and where thieves dig through and steal; but store up for yourselves treasures in the heavens.' Do you store up in heaven? yourself you are the cause of your name being written in the heavens. These things because of 'Let them be written upon the earth.' And he gives the cause: 'Because they have forsaken the fountain of life the Lord.' And in the beginning the same prophet spoke from the face of God: 'Me they have forsaken the fountain of waters of life,' and now: 'They have forsaken the fountain of life the Lord.' Let us say also we, if we are willing not to forsake the fountain of life the Lord, the voice of the genuine sons of Jesus disciples, which they have said to the teacher saying to them: 'Not and you wish to go'? What then shall we say? 'Lord, to where shall we go?' You have the words of eternal life. Here also the second section ended.
source_text: recipias: «si quis« inquit «videtur sibi sapiens esse in vobis in isto saeculo, stultus fiat« (vgl. I Kor.3,18). Solvit qui ante clamavit: stultus esto et fatuus, ut sapiens fias (vielleicht besser Rabanus: Attende quia non solum non clamavit: stultus esto et fatuus, sed ut sapiens fias. Statt: Solvit qui ante haben Hss.: Solum quia non) Si itaque est quaedam sapientia culpabilis, juxta quam «filii saeculi hujus sapientiores sunt a filiis lucis in generatione ista« (vgl. Luk. 16,8), bonus est Deus, qui tiores sunt a filiis lucis in generatione ista« (vgl. Luk.16,8), bonus est Deus, qui contrariis diversa subvertit, ut faciat compleri id quod dictum est: «novissimum ejus erit insipiens. Quando novissimum ejus erit insipiens? Oportet Christum «regnare, usque dum ponat omnes inimicos ejus Deus sub pedibus ejus«, cum autem omnia ei subjecerit, «novissimus inimicus destruetur mors« (vgl.I Kor.15, 25.26); cum destruta fuerit mors, tune extrema perdicis erunt, et novissimum ejus fiet insipiens.
